## About

These Python (Jupyter) cells open in lightbox, without panzoom. The [panzoom
version](k-jupyter-auto.html) has the same cases with `panzoom: true`.
Compare each case with the same number there. The knitr equivalents are the
R [lightbox version](a-lightbox.html) and [global panzoom
version](c-panzoom-auto.html).

```yaml
lightbox: true
```

Jupyter leaves the `panzoom` and `lightbox` options out of the code shown
on the page; the **Code** button at the top shows the full source.

The cases below share this setup:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
```

## 1. Figure with a caption {#c1 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "A Python figure with a caption. It opens in lightbox."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.show()
```

## 2. Plot without a caption {#c2 expect-open="glightbox"}

A plot without a caption. It opens in lightbox.

```{python}
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x))
plt.show()
```

## 3. Subfigures {#c3 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{python}
#| label: fig-pair
#| fig-cap: "Two subfigures from one cell. They open in lightbox as a two-image gallery."
#| fig-subcap: ["Sine", "Cosine"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

plt.plot(x, np.sin(2 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(2 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 4. lightbox options {#c4 expect-open="glightbox"}

Two cells with `lightbox:` options for a group and a description. With
Jupyter, lightbox ignores the options themselves, so each opens in lightbox
on its own, without the group or description.

```{python}
#| lightbox:
#|   group: waves
#|   description: "Ignored by lightbox with Jupyter."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(3 * x))
plt.show()
plt.plot(x, np.cos(3 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 5. lightbox off {#c5 expect-open="nothing"}

```{python}
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `lightbox: false`. Clicking it does nothing."

plt.plot(x, np.sin(4 * x))
plt.show()
```

## 6. panzoom on a cell {#c6 expect-open="glightbox"}

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: "A cell with `panzoom: true`. The panzoom filter isn't loaded here, so the option means nothing, and the plot opens in lightbox."

plt.plot(x, np.cos(4 * x))
plt.show()
```
